answer.label: fine-tune bias
answer.justification: Only logit-level measurements are available, and they match the fine-tune bias fingerprint closely: KL 0.071 (document 0.082), TV 0.076 (0.082), top-1 agreement 0.938 (0.935), sequence agreement 0.562 (0.583) and Token-DiFR gap 0.226 (0.219). The deciding value is the raw-score shift ÷ TV of 11.5 ×10⁵. Only fine-tune bias reaches about 10 ×10⁵; every other class falls between 2.3 and 3.9. Quantization is the nearest alternative on KL, but its top-1 agreement (0.951), Token-DiFR gap (0.038) and raw-score shift (2.3) all fit worse. The fine-tune backdoor has a higher KL (0.15) and a raw-score shift of 3.3. Both system-prompt classes have far larger KL (0.24–0.30) and lower top-1 agreement (0.87–0.89). None is ruled out because the values are non-zero. Confidence is not higher because output and activation levels were not measured, so the call rests on logit features alone.
